# Dreamcast native port: history

The arcade-side and Dreamcast-side record of the port, newest first, as it was kept in the root
`HANDOFF.md` while the work was done. The current state is in `HANDOFF.md` next to this file.

## The gear indicator (18 October 2026, branch gear-hud)

The arcade's own gear indicator b0c0 (manual races) is native: the H-gate lever animates for 31 ticks after
a shift, then "(n)" over "SHIFT", right of the speed (the 2001 Dreamcast version's icon is this lever art).
Checked against an m2segment --trace-hud of the manual race: 10148 frames equal (lever 526, digit 9612), 2
one tick stale, both on the reference's variables and on the native race; manual lockstep PASS; make check
77 PASS and the 5 known FAIL lines. Options: NATIVE_HUD_GEAR_GATE=1 (H-gate always, the 2001 look),
NATIVE_HUD_GEAR_AUTO=1 (automatic races too). Needs a HUD pack from this prepare_hud.py (four sheets; an
older pack draws no indicator). Details: platform/dreamcast-native/HANDOFF.md, "18 October: the gear indicator".
Not to re-propose: a new texture or palette bank for a Dreamcast-made gear icon (the arcade has the art);
a separate digital km/h (b1a4 draws it already).

## Dreamcast sound, slice 2 (17 October 2026)

Every race command the original sends is now native and checked against fresh m2segment
--trace-sound references with compare_race_sound.py --all: fast race 777/777, manual 938/938, slot
A/B 778/778, damage E 1878/1878 and G 1797/1797; damage A, C, F, H equal but for the results entry
past the harness window (results.c sends it) and 9e1d (the debris actors at 223xxx, not native). New
gameplay-state writes, as the original's: 9148's lane 501a04 = 2/6 (wall rub, race_sound.c's draw
hook), 35b0's 501a02 = 28/29 at 640/385 left and a900's 501a02 = 30 per wrong-way tick
(race_scene.h), 503690 = frame parity for the crash end's 41/42; row 30's specials use the board's
unit setting 1. Lockstep damage/pit/slot/negspeed/manual PASS, fuzz 0 rejected; the slot test pins
the event sink's new counts (81 -> 108, fast race 80 -> 107). Sound-only code stays in race_sound.c
/ sfx.c (-fno-lto); race_sound.c also gets the gameplay float flags (its distances match the
harness's). Announcer: recipes/README.md "Sound effects" measures both options; streaming is
NATIVE_SFX_VOICE_STREAM=1 with sfx/voices.pak (build_sfx.sh's default output), resident is
build_sfx.sh --voices resident with the soundtrack in ADPCM. The choice is made by ear.

## Operator settings and VMU records 2026-10-17

Branch rules (details: platform/dreamcast-native/HANDOFF.md, "17 October: operator settings and VMU records").
The EEPROM layout and boot check 227cf0 are decoded; GAME ASSIGNMENTS has DIFFICULTY, ADVERTISE SOUND,
COUNTRY, CABINET and the coin items, nothing else. Difficulty (the start time and the awards) and
advertise sound are native settings; the difficulty is lockstep-checked against races recorded with
m2segment --nvram and tools/settings_eeprom.py (fast race x3, time-outs x3, ninth place). The three
record tables are course 0 Beginner 1d00360, 1 Expert 1d005a0, 2/3 Advanced 1d007e0 (226a5c), and the
native defaults equal the original's backup RAM after the boot (check_save_reference.c, m2segment
--save-nvram). Records and settings are saved to the VMU (DAYTONA93NAT, 5 blocks) on a KOS thread after
the name entry and from the settings screen (title: both triggers + START); test_game_save.c runs the
store against a fake VMU. Not on hardware yet.
Not to re-propose: a race-length (laps) operator setting for daytona93 (there is none: laps are table
03950[course]); taking COUNTRY or CABINET as gameplay settings (no simulation reader; texts, voices, mph
and colour tables only).

## Dreamcast sound effects, first slice 2026-10-17

Branch sfx. The effects come from the ROM set (recipes/build_sfx.sh, step `sfx`
of build_assets.sh for a .zip set): the native sequencer renders every effect
command into a MultiPCM VGM, AICAforge afx_vgm/afx_bank make one race bank
(62 flows: ten engine layers as controlled flows, the channel-14 kit, THREE TWO
ONE GO, crowd, slot machine; 485,984 bytes of AICA RAM, 25,050 left beside the
race recording t03). code/audio/sfx.c plays them; include/race_sound.h derives
the original's gameplay-driven commands (19c58 rpm, 19d1c slip, ab78 start
voices, 134f8 lap cues, 9888 rear skid, 158c8 player spin, the be1700/be1900
resets) without writing gameplay state; event-tail and pit cues now honour the
19bdc gate (nothing after phase 22). Checked against the original's UART trace
(m2segment --trace-sound): fast race be17 311/311, be19 173/173, ae21 40/40,
ae20 8/8, skids exact; damage run E spin 2/2, be17 1497/1497.
Not yet: announcer phrases other than the countdown (913 KB in ADPCM, no room
beside t03), wall rub 9e0b/9e0c (9148 writes intent lane 501a04 = 2/6, not
native), time-out beeps 9e0d/9e0e (35b0, tables 231e48/231e60), opponents'
spins (15b90, TGP distance -> 235a38/235a58), crashes 9e08/9e0a/9e1b/16790,
be34/be35 (TGP), be37 (9110), the 99xx positional passes (19590).
Manual races (after the gearbox merge): no command of the original's depends on
the transmission; the manual race matches like the fast one (be17 418/418, be19
202/202), but for ae2125 at remaining == 640 (35b0 signal 28, not native yet).
Heap: the stats ELF has 3,154,144 free while the scene runs (budget 3,145,728;
3,181,184 before the effects): the bank costs 17,280 of heap, the code about 9.8 KB.
Scripted builds compile name entry out (results.c) so LTO's inlining cannot bring it back.
Frame time (after the views merge, 063b1d5): rebased on ed98455 the stats ELF lost 0.24 ms of
registration a frame on hardware (7.54 -> 7.78) with the same work. Cause: placement. Under
NATIVE_LTO=one any change inside the unit (three calls in sound.c were enough) changes GCC's inlining
and emission order, and the hot sq_* functions land on other I-cache lines (static check: 9 of 32 hot
registration functions at the baseline's relative index; the data reordered too). The race sound hooks
and sfx.c are now outside the unit (race_sound.c, -fno-lto), which is not enough on its own; for an
A/B the sfx ELF is linked with tools/pin_layout.py's ordering file from the baseline's map (two links):
32/32 registration functions and every .rodata/.data/.bss section at the baseline offsets, the data
moved by exactly 8 KiB as a whole. Left: the effects' 17 KB of heap before the assets (896 bytes mod
16 KiB against .bss), and practice_update's own inlining. Scripts: build/dc-native-sfx.elf/build3.sh,
pin_pair.sh. A general fix would be an LTO hot order for every build.
Not to re-propose: stopping the previous sequence of a track on a new start
(the board lets a replaced sequence's voices sound on); judging one-shot
length from the sequencer's note-off (MultiPCM samples always loop: a silent
loop marks a one-shot).

## Static front-facing world materials cache their binding, 2026-10-06

`nm_render_world_attach` now allocates one 32-byte-aligned `uint16_t` binding
cache per world face (about 10 KiB for the current course), filled only for the
existing positive static-luma faces. Direct SQ submission reads that cache only
when a DNM4 normal cone has proven the whole group front-facing;
uncertain/rear/two-sided paths retain the normal material/luma lookup. This
removes the large `material*256+luma` table read from that static hot path
without changing texture residency or PVR headers. The host SQ fixture and full
Dreamcast check pass; startup stream parity and hardware timing remain the
necessary target evidence.

## Normal-cone center lengths are attach-time cached, 2026-10-06

The DNM4 normal-group record's final serialized-zero slot is now a float
`normal_length`. The reader rejects nonzero input; `nm_render_world_attach`
calculates the conservative SH4ZAM FIPR/FSRRA length exactly once for each cone
group, like its existing static face-luma cache. Frame-time cone facing
therefore no longer calculates that length. The unchanged current DNM4 pack
passes the current reader and 32 malformed-pack cases. Normal and
`NATIVE_BOUNDS_VERIFY` handopt ELFs rebuild, but the FTRV cone oracle and
performance result still await a hardware loader.

## Model-space normal-cone classification awaits hardware oracle, 2026-10-06

The normal-cone test formerly used two FTRVs for every visible DNM4 group to
classify facing. `nm_scenery_normal_group_view` now converts the rigid camera
translation to model space once per shared scenery frame; `sq_normal_group_facing`
uses the equivalent SH4ZAM dot/FSRRA expression without those group FTRVs. The
existing `NATIVE_BOUNDS_VERIFY` mode retains the old FTRV calculation and aborts
if its `-1/0/+1` classification differs. This is compiled, and the host SQ fixture
verifies the rigid-transform identity, but it has **not** run on hardware or
received a performance claim yet.

## SH4ZAM lighting is no longer a product option, 2026-10-05

`NATIVE_LIGHT_FIPR` was always enabled by the normal direct-SQ Dreamcast
build, so it selected no supported product behavior. It is removed. Target
code now selects SH4ZAM vector dots and specialized static-world lighting with
`__DREAMCAST__`; host checks retain the scalar reference implementation. The
optional `NATIVE_LIGHT_VERIFY` diagnostic still requires its direct-SQ path.
`test_practice_render_split.py` rejects the retired selector.

## Normal-cone groups now also skip per-face facing transforms, 2026-10-05

DNM4's existing offline normal cone is now named for what it is rather than
only its original use: it conservatively proves a world group entirely rear,
entirely front, or uncertain. A front proof skips the two per-face FTRVs and
facing dot that static-world lighting otherwise needs for camera orientation;
the precomputed per-face diffuse result is retained, so the group does not
flatten visible lighting. The resident normal-cone counters now report both
rear rejects and front-facing skips at renderer release. `NATIVE_BOUNDS_VERIFY`
remains the hardware oracle: it recomputes the generic face result and fails
if a group labelled front contains a rear-facing face.

The serialized bit stays `1`, preserving all DNM4 assets; the public symbol is
now `NM_NORMAL_GROUP_CONE`. The SQ host fixture and normal Dreamcast build need
to pass before treating this as a hardware performance gain.

## Static scenery light stays in model space, 2026-10-05

normal cones for world-only early backface rejection. The regular scenery

claim is made until that verifier and timing run on the console.

## Native title-to-cinematic attract mode, 2026-10-05

The ordinary title now enters the existing authored `nm_intro_scene` after
20 seconds rather than only displaying a static title indefinitely. The mode
releases the title PAL4 resources before loading the usual course renderer,
runs the existing 20/21-car cinematic simulation for 1,800 fixed ticks, then
releases course resources and returns to title. START/A during the cinematic
goes directly to the ordinary controllable 40-car race. No parallel scene,
physics or renderer was added.

`RACE_ASSET_DIR` replaces the misleading `NATIVE_INTRO_DIR` build input; it

the old implicit 1200-tick stop is gone; finite runs must opt in with a limit.

removed from the game path. The direct-SQ TA budget guard remains mandatory.

`build/dc-native-race-unconditional-check/bin/daytona-native-driving-3d-textured-world-resident-car.elf`.

inspection, SH4ZAM matrix-load cases, quad/strip and SQ-capacity fixture,

## Native boot/title return mode, 2026-10-05

The game now boots into the existing offline-prepared no-credit Daytona title,
instead of allocating course textures before a title exists. `title_render.c`
owns its 27 resident textures, 14 PAL4 banks and cached OP/PT headers (163840
bytes VRAM); it queues one callback per PVR list and emits directly through
`pvr_dr_target`. The immutable generated title data remains selected by
`TITLE_SCENE_DIR`, not a `NATIVE_*` source switch.

`title_mode.c` is a normal enDjinn mode. START or A first fences/releases only
the title assets, then invokes the existing race reset/detail/render path.
After Name Entry, `name_mode` now returns to this title instead of terminating
the engine. A global exit chord still terminates instead of silently changing
screen; the host lifecycle test covers both return-to-title and that failure
boundary. `AUTO_START=1` is a finite-test build option only; it bypasses the
title without changing production flow.

## Hardware-verified DNM4 normal-cone face batches, 2026-10-05

`prepare_models.py --face-group-size 32` now writes DNM4 rather than DNM3:
it retains spatial bounds and source-face order, but splits only sufficiently
large, wholly one-sided spatial blocks by a 30-degree normal cone. Each 64-byte
group has a mean normal/deviation sphere and the facing-point sphere used by
the existing supplied-normal path. DNM1/2/3 remain loadable. The reader checks
all new floats, radii, flags, padding, mesh ownership and bounds; Python and C
pack tests reject corrupted cone metadata.

The direct-SQ world path uses SH4ZAM XMTRX/FIPR/FSRRA primitives to reject a
cone only with a conservative upper bound. It falls back to the original
per-face code for non-isometric/uncertain/two-sided groups. A temporary
`shz_vec4_magnitude` formulation stalled the target; the retained path uses
validated positive squared lengths plus `shz_inv_sqrtf`, inflated by 0.1%.
The `NATIVE_BOUNDS_VERIFY` target recomputes the original face light/cull for
each group-rejected face and aborts on any mismatch.

Fresh DNM4 world pack `build/dc-native-normal-groups.DTarNN/world.dnm`:
478416 bytes, 263 spatial/orientation groups, 64 cone candidates. Hardware
verify session57493 passed all existing startup oracles and 1200 ticks with
zero cone-cull failures; 78 group /624 face rejects over899 render frames.
Quiet same-ELF A/B: DNM3 18.988ms mean vs DNM4 18.899ms mean, so the single
run suggests no regression but is not enough to claim a speedup. DNM4 did
reject95 groups/760 faces over1105 frames. Both returned0 to loader. No CDI or
published runtime mount changed.

## Hardware-verified name entry and fixed DcTx label dimensions, 2026-10-05

The generic ROM-label packer had written literal texture dimensions to the DcTx
header but always wrote PVR type low bits `0x12` (32x32). That silently
misdescribed cropped 64/128px label textures. enDjinn correctly reported the
first name background as 32x32 when the generated header declared 128x128.

power-of-two allocation; `test_result_labels.py` independently checks both
literal and PVR dimensions for every emitted DcTx. This applies to result and
name labels. Result loader's raw-header validation now derives the same bits.

## Resident geometry preparation now runs in object callbacks, 2026-10-05

Console remains OFF. sq_prepare_batch is the extracted SAME
face-light/material-selection/projected cache arithmetic, reused by eager
streaming/startup and lazy resident rendering. sq_prepare_source now admits
bounded batch storage and performs instance AABB culling only in the resident
path. First object callback prepares its parts once; later PT reuses their
face/point caches. Resident preparation performs no texture pin/demand marking,
header scan/compilation, upload or resource wait. All headers/textures were
initialized before this route is selected. Streaming still prepares/resolves
resources before any PVR callback; no unsafe deferral.

Removed the whole-scene practice_render_frame callback. Gameplay's render
enqueue now builds instance poses/coarse bounds, then queues objects before
enDjinn's wait. Shared reflection UV update, camera and model-part pose setup
remain in scene setup; do not claim absolutely all presentation work is lazy.
Faces/vertices are processed in the object's callback. Both OP/PT callbacks
are queued for each coarse-visible lazy object to preserve original PT/HUD
ordering without examining faces early; an empty list emits nothing. Culling
inside an object can thus leave a cheap empty callback. No per-polygon calls.

Batch descriptors are64bytes on SH4 (static assertion), allocated32-aligned.
Instance is resolved from the existing source/index, no redundant pointer or
new frame allocation. Part bounds classification is retained; group planes
are reconstructed inside preparation only when needed. SQ quad strips retained.

## Per-car/per-list callbacks replace two global submission calls, 2026-10-05

Confirmed: intended enDjinn organization: one game object (car) queues a
function/data pair per relevant list, with ALL its body/window/wheel/shadow/
damage parts batched inside that call. Not one callback per mesh or polygon, and
not one global OP/PT pair for the whole world. Console remains OFF.

Implemented first stage: render/practice.c records 45 car-part boundaries
(44 cars plus sentinel); preserves detail order and special/culled-car parts.
nm_render_enqueue_objects borrows those boundaries. Direct SQ batches retain
original instance index/source and first batch holds object range length.
sq_queue_objects groups surviving car parts across culled holes, skips empty
lists, and queues each scenery instance separately. OP/PT share the object's
borrowed data pointer. sq_emit_range renders only its batch range, retaining
quad strips, vertex attributes and source order. Each callback explicitly emits
its initial cached header; no unsafe TA-state assumption across object calls.
No new per-frame allocation or engine/PC/asset change. Single-player fallback
groups all car parts. Old non-direct diagnostics keep their existing submission.

IMPORTANT: this is not the finished architecture. sq_prepare still performs
global face lighting/transform/cache/resource work BEFORE object callbacks.
Resident practice_prepare itself is deferred in OP, but that does not satisfy
the desired per-object work boundary. Next split coarse instance setup from
per-object preparation, then move the latter into object callbacks while
preserving shared OP/PT caches and streaming upload fences. Do not claim all
geometry is now lazy or that callbacks already borrow raw gameplay objects.

## Detail classification/order slices verified, 2026-10-05

Order is ONE backward adjacent pass, preserving ties; not full sort. Original
depth storage is signed16; production caller MUST range-check fresh transformed
depths before narrowing and retain old depth on excluded cells. Do not claim

## Original base-reset clearing extent verified, 2026-10-05

Inspection of e3f4 base reset revealed an important non-memset behavior:
r15=entity+52, r14 based on entity-size word8; e414..e41c repeatedly writes STQ to
SAME r15, never advances the address. Therefore only entity34..43 are zeroed by
that loop, not all car state. Explicit later stores e420..e590 reset other fields,
preserving remaining old fields/shared state. Do NOT implement base reset as
player={0} or whole-car memset: would erase wheel phases/other state and
misrepresent restart behavior.

## Correct active-CPU versus wall-time profiling, 2026-10-04

KOS perfctr.h explicitly documents perf_cntr_timer_ns as ACTIVE CPU time:
it stops while the kernel sleeps. DRAW_PHASE_* uses this clock, whereas

## Offline DNM3 face groups integrated, 2026-10-04

DNM3 extends DNM2: header.reserved=group count, mesh.padding[0:2] =first/count,
face.padding=absolute group, zero-align position refs to4, append 24-byte float
bounds/group. Existing padding supplies mapping, not extra arrays. Old DNM1/2
stay accepted. Reader validates contiguous mesh group ranges, counts, finite
ordered bounds inside mesh, every face reference, every member vertex inside its
group's bounds, zero alignment and exact file/2MiB size limits.

Renderer reuses conservative nm_bounds_visible before face lighting/vertex
demand. Shared491-byte scratch holds visibility; culled face light sentinel-2
skips subsequent material/clip work. No per-frame allocation/reordering, no new
PVR lifecycle, no change to precision, SQ, SH4ZAM or PC reference. Startup full
uncached stream remains oracle (ignores grouping). Grouping is optional by pack.

New `prepare_material_crops.py` reuses source/VQ validation and crops existing
VQ index maps, retaining codebooks and verifying every decoded crop texel/alpha

per original resource (including the estimated 32-byte allocation overhead).

resources are deduplicated. No global packing/optimality claim.

`m2segment --export-native-cells NEW_DIR` now loads all 256 authored cells of
the currently selected table, captures a visible scenery object's render state,
then decodes EVERY table object through an isolated reference `Geo` snapshot.
It owns copies of mutable geometry/raster RAM and borrows ROM/pages only while
the original owner is alive. The existing source-mesh decoder checks transforms,
topology and face lighting against reference words. This is host-only reuse,
not another geometry parser or target simulation. All sampled meshes AND their
instance contexts must match the complete export; partial or inconsistent samples
fail instead of silently being described as complete scenery.

Source provenance rechecked with `i960dis`: 0x380c reads selector 0x501460;

mask 15 per axis, then x+16*z. Nominal cells are 128 units across; exact FP
rounding/boundary rules and physical units are not yet a native gameplay gate.

**Native projection/clipping kernel, 2026-10-03 (preceding milestone).**
`code/geometry.h/.c` now provides allocation-free triangle projection, five
homogeneous clipping planes (four sides, then positive near), finite guards,
perspective UV/depth attributes, and a reusable per-instance vertex cache.
Source quads are split into fans. Validate a camera once with `nm_view_valid`
before cached operations; never reuse cache entries under another camera.
Only intersected triangles use double intermediates; ordinary classification
and projection are float, with one reciprocal per projected vertex. Raw UV
units can be cached and the perspective attributes scaled per material later.

The host check covers **105,205 triangles**, including 100,000 synthetic cases
spanning six depth orders and eye-plane crossings plus all **5192 triangles**
from the local pack. An independent double oracle checks cyclic vertex order,
coordinates, q/uq/vq, and viewport bounds; 401 offset cases also check the old
PVR adapter's projection conventions. Cached/uncached outputs are byte-equal,
as are raw-UV postscaling and prescaled-UV paths for the real pack. Maximum
coordinate error is **5.43459e-5 logical pixels**, scaled attribute error
**1.78671e-7** (gates 0.02 pixels / 2e-4). Seven focused CTests and ASan/UBSan
pass. This is kernel validation, NOT full reference culling/window-priority,
master-Z, lighting, textured pixels, TGP or gameplay parity.

Hardware diagnostic now also checks a ROM-free near-plane case and times five
passes over the source meshes using real SH4ZAM transforms. Counts agree with
host: 5192 triangles, **3801 frustum survivors**, 11,472 output vertices.
Host path inventory: 3673 trivial accepts, 1391 trivial rejects, 128 clips.
No backface/object/sector culling is applied yet. Vertex scratch is **43,692

## Offline Dreamcast assets, first notes (early October 2026)

**Offline Dreamcast assets (in progress).** `m2segment --export-textures NEW_DIR`
now decodes a selected frame's base textures with full material headers,
8-bit luminance, and its live palette/luma/colour-translation state.
`scripts/prepare_dreamcast_textures.py` invokes installed pvrtex for twiddled
VQ RGB565/ARGB1555 (default), exact PAL4 or VQ-PAL4, deduplicates identical
source images and writes verified DcTx manifests with actual upload sizes.
All generated images/assets stay ignored. ROM-free decoding tests compare
synthetic texel centres against the existing reference rasterizer, including
sheet folding; parser tests reject malformed DcTx data. This does not yet
bind textures in the console renderer, handle original mip/microtextures,
cover all material states, or preprocess models. Baked lighting is explicit,
not a licence to replay recorded geometry or frames.

The initial automatic PAL4 quantizer changed four pixels in texture 188 of
the frame-183 export despite <=16 source colours. The encoder now supplies
an explicit, canonical exact DPAL palette; never assume max-color=16 alone
is lossless. Count palette banks as well as texture bytes before selecting
PAL4/VQ-PAL4: 64 banks is the hardware limit, with UI sharing that budget.
All 315 unique lossless PAL4 previews from frame 183 now compare pixel-exact
against the decoded source TGAs. `--format mixed` uses VQ-PAL4 for the largest
textures up to 48 banks by default (16 left for UI), VQ RGB565/ARGB1555 for
the rest; identical canonical palettes share banks. It is a size heuristic,
not a quality classifier or a complete stage working-set allocator.
Prepared local assets are under `build/dc-assets.OAop1S/`: frame183-ready
has 358 material mappings / 315 unique textures, 1,241,536 bytes PVR payload,
48 palette banks; beginner3000-ready has 312 / 293, 508,928 bytes and 48
banks. These include enDjinn DcTx files, DPAL palettes, PNG previews and
manifests with hashes/bank assignments. Both sample payloads fit the planned
1,498,368-byte texture budget, not proof a whole stage fits. The all-VQ
frame183 version needs 1,831,360 bytes; all-VQ-PAL4 needs 677,824 bytes but
313 banks, so neither uniform choice meets both limits for that sample.
ROM-free asset/reference-raster and DcTx/palette tests passed; the SH-4
build check passed. These new assets have not yet been loaded/drawn on
hardware. The prior kos-tool session ended with status 143; no reset or
new upload was made during asset preparation.

`--profile-rom` now counts successful cache hits and misses per frame, not
just misses. The 6,000-frame race_basic run still matched every resident
frame (651,831 misses). ROM-page unions: all 5.004 MiB, boot/title/attract
4.199 MiB, credit 0.785 MiB, selects 1.285 MiB, beginner race 2.055 MiB.
Peak simultaneous per-frame ROM pages total 0.863 MiB. These are touched
raw-ROM pages, not final preprocessed pack sizes, and the ranges are script
transitions rather than validated screen/state boundaries.

**Dreamcast silent native build (3 Oct 2026, in progress).** The separate
enDjinn frontend now instantiates the existing GameLoop and advances it in
the mode updater, with controller input latched through enDjinn; PVR
callbacks only present completed Video state. Generated i960 and TGP code
are cross-compiled, no reference sound board is selected, and SH4ZAM stays
in presentation transforms. The ROM-free fixture remains selectable with
`DAYTONA_GAME=0`. Hardware now boots the native game and presents actual 3D:
HDMI capture shows frame 183 with 1,707 polygons, road and scenery. The
43,484 ms simulation time for that earlier direct-mapped-cache frame is nowhere near playable speed;
textures, UI composition and production ordering are not implemented.
Do not call this playable or a completed Dreamcast port. The first -O2 ELF occupied 7,620,693
bytes of text and failed allocating 2 MiB during startup; -Os reduced text
to 3,288,697 bytes and paging the program image allowed startup to complete.

Bounded caches cover program/main_data/copro_data/polygon/texture images (64 KiB
each, 320 KiB payload plus about 75 KiB metadata), now fully associative LRU
with O(1) inverse-map hits. Mapped-only page banks replace the flat page
table. GPU-only Video construction omits CPU composition/raster targets,
which are restored lazily when software output is selected. Free-run
Lockstep callbacks recycle slots and release consumed captures rather than
growing for the entire race. Five ROM-free checks passed: page-cache
eviction/wrap/short-read handling, Geo clipping/streaming, budget arithmetic,
and callback capture release plus GPU-to-CPU buffer restoration.

Measured on the PC: paged and resident silent runtimes matched screen hash,
i960/TGP instruction counts and IRQ count at every frame through the
6,000-frame race_basic replay. 196,665,345 i960 instructions, 223,429,779
TGP instructions, final screen hash ad67233983ea8808, 651,831 page misses
with LRU versus 2,534,835 with the earlier direct-mapped cache at the same

This validates cache semantics, not new MAME parity or SH-4 floating-point
parity. Stage source counts remain 4bpp base-level estimates; peak source

Findings / do not re-propose: the supplied archive lacks the required
sound-program revision; `m2import --no-sound` verifies every game ROM and
explicitly omits audio instead of substituting another sound revision.
Generators need pre-created output directories: an earlier call without
them reported success but wrote no sources. `kos-tool -m` mounts `/pc/`,
not `/cd/`. KOS's libstdc++ configuration does not expose std::snprintf;
the affected runtime calls use the available global C function. The first
GPU-buffer test caught missing lazy raster allocation on a software frame
with 3D disabled; software composition now restores the target too.
The frontend incorrectly set no_soft_reset=true despite using the enDjinn
loop; that override is removed and the build check prevents recurrence.
The physical START+A+B+X+Y chord returned zero to kos-tool; the next upload
verified an idle loader without restarting. Heap and frame-stage
diagnostics located the RAM failure at frame 182: polygon-vector growth
needed 409,600 bytes while retaining its old 204,800-byte buffer. The heap
had 215,976 free bytes and could not extend by the requested amount. The
native frontend now disables its unused decoded CPU tile cache (3 MiB),

restores the cache and matches reference output. The new console run has
2,908,680 free heap bytes at frame 120 (formerly 221,824), with video time
below the millisecond clock resolution (formerly 142 ms). Hardware now
passes the failing frame 182 and presents actual geometry at frame 183.
This does not prove a full race fits; System24 PVR composition remains required.
No board/TGP result has been
silently approximated. Native generated instruction code still retains guest
register and board-interface work; this is not the desired final SH-4 cost.

The earlier 4.578 MiB texture-cache budget was wrong: it omitted KOS TA allocations. Accounting for
both vertex/OPB/tile sets with enDjinn defaults, the original 16-bit scanout/composite/UI/slack
assumptions left 2,112,768 bytes (2.015 MiB). The required 24-bit packed RGB888 scanout uses

Dithering is explicitly disabled. The mixed-format plan is exact 4bpp UI, VQ-4bpp for suitable
